mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent 1% monthly increase in both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 1% in 1 month, the S&P 500 60-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates, which increases discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.0% y/y.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes lower corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 jobs indicates robust labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rise > 150k.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.5% per annum signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% and a rise in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 150,000 signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0 and PAYEMS rise > 150k in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0 and PAYEMS rise > 150k.
